stem.en: A farmer grows one crop from cuttings of a single plant. A new disease arrives that this plant cannot resist. Why is this a risk?

text.en: There is no variation, so all plants share it.

feedback.en: Yes. Whatever harms one plant can harm them all.

text.en: Cuttings always have weaker roots than seedlings.

feedback.en: Cuttings grow their own roots. The risk is sameness, not weak roots.

text.en: Each plant will soon change into a new variety.

feedback.en: Cuttings stay genetically identical to their parent.

text.en: Too many different kinds now grow side by side.

feedback.en: The field holds one kind only, and that is the risk.

explanation.en: A field of cuttings has no variation. If the plant cannot resist a disease, none of the copies can.

hints.en: How many different kinds of plant are in this field?
Does a cutting differ from its parent?
